Assessment
CLINICAL SUMMARY & ICHD-3 CLASSIFICATION:
Jerica Barton (DOB 1964-05-16, MRN SYN-5044832) is a 60-year-old female of Han Chinese ancestry (born in Fujian province, China) with a 3-month history of recurrent, unilateral paroxysmal facial pain in the right cheek and upper lip (right maxillary/V2 distribution). Attacks consist of severe, electric-shock-like stabs lasting 1-2 seconds, occurring 20-40 times/day, precipitated by innocuous stimuli (brushing teeth, chewing, light touch of the cheek, cold wind), with complete freedom from pain between attacks. Prior extraction of tooth #3 (2024-03-04) and a 4-week trial of gabapentin up to 900 mg/day (stopped due to dizziness and lack of efficacy) provided no relief. Dental exam confirmed normal healing and no odontogenic pathology. Neurological exam is normal, including intact facial sensation, normal corneal reflexes, and intact hearing. Baseline labs (2024-05-21) are normal (Na 139 mmol/L, Cr 0.7 mg/dL, ALT 19 U/L, Platelets 236 x10^3/uL).

ICHD-3 Diagnostic Classification:
- 13.1.1 Trigeminal neuralgia (TN), right V2 (maxillary) division, purely paroxysmal phenotype.
- Meets all ICHD-3 criteria for TN: (A) Recurrent paroxysms
